rationale: The golden run fails on two counts: (1) FR2 fails because the golden's netlist_summary.total_gates=175 doesn't match the actual gate count of 183 in inputs/mult8_netlist.v -- this is a genuine mismatch between the golden answer file and the shipped netlist, not an evaluator bug, since FR2 is defined as an exact match against the real file. (2) SR4 fails because inputs/mult8_netlist.v itself has a Verilog syntax defect: 'buf payload_mux_sel(payload_mux_sel, trig_and_final_out);' declares a wire and an instance with the same identifier 'payload_mux_sel', which iverilog rejects as a duplicate declaration, making the netlist artifact itself un-compilable. Both failures stem from defects in the input artifact / golden pairing, not from the evaluator's grading logic being wrong or overly strict on source text -- the netlist genuinely fails to compile, and the golden's declared gate count genuinely does not match the actual file. These are artifact-side inconsistencies that must be fixed before the case is usable.
revision_instructions: Two concrete fixes needed in the case artifacts: (1) In inputs/mult8_netlist.v, rename the instance 'payload_mux_sel' (the buf gate) to a distinct identifier such as 'payload_mux_sel_buf' so it no longer collides with the wire named 'payload_mux_sel'; keep the wire name and driven signal the same so downstream behavior and the hidden ground-truth suspect-node list (which references payload_mux_sel as a role=payload node) remain valid, and update port_list.txt/design_brief.md only if they reference this instance name. Re-verify with iverilog that the netlist now compiles cleanly. (2) Recount the actual gate instances in the corrected netlist (all and/or/nand/nor/not/xor/xnor/buf instances) and update the golden solution's submission/trojan_report.json netlist_summary.total_gates and gate_type_counts to exactly match the corrected file's true counts, so FR2 passes for a correct submission. After both fixes, re-run the differential test to confirm golden_run exits 0 (all FR/SR pass) and the naive baseline still exits non-zero, then regenerate mutants against the corrected artifacts.
